text:
Alex Liu: Hey @people-ops — got my final paycheck and the PTO cashout looks wrong. I moved to the Netherlands in Aug 2025 and my residency should be NL for year-end tax. PTO cashout was €1,200 but taxes withheld look like full US rate (~45%) instead of NL treaty rate. Can someone take a look?
Maria Gomez: Hi Alex — sorry about that, can you DM your employee ID and the paystub screenshot? We'll pull the pay run. Also, did you file the Dutch tax residency docs with relocation onboarding?
Alex Liu: Employee ID 52378. Screenshot pasted in DM (saw it uploaded to you). I did submit the relocation packet but not the treaty form separately — thought payroll would pick it up from People Ops.
Jordan Patel: looping in payroll. @Maria: if residency wasn't propagated to payroll system before the run, it's likely defaulted to US withholding. We can do a retro adjustment if payroll confirms. Alex, can you confirm your NL BSN was added to ADP?
Alex Liu: BSN is 12-34-56-78. I uploaded it in the onboarding form on Sep 2, 2025. Happy to forward any receipts. :slightly_smiling_face:
PayrollBot: Automated note: pay run 2025-12-14 processed. Adjustment window open for 5 business days. Reference PR# 2025-12-14-52378.
Maria Gomez: Thanks. Jordan — can you check whether the pay run used the 'US tax resident' flag? If so, we need a tax reclass and then issue a corrected final pay and a corrected W-2 (or W-2c) / local NL jaaropgaaf as applicable. Alex, we'll need your relocation confirmation email attached for audit.
Jordan Patel: On it. Quick check of the run shows `tax_residency=US` for ID 52378. Looks like the residency change in Workday didn't sync before the cut. We'll request a tax reclassification and run a retro calculation to refund excess US withholding and apply NL rates. That will generate a corrected wage statement.
Alex Liu: Appreciate it. Timeline? I need to confirm with my tax advisor before year-end.
Maria Gomez: We'll aim to submit the reclass today. Expect an internal payroll ticket + confirmation here within 48 hours. If the correction changes taxable wages reported to US, we'll coordinate with tax team on whether a W-2c is needed. If it's strictly withholding correction with same gross, might be a payroll refund + local reporting.
Jordan Patel: Created ticket #PAY-7892 and marked for expedited handling. Payroll ops will try to include the adjustment in the next off-cycle. If we can't, we'll do a manual refund and then the year-end correction. We'll post updates in this thread. :white_check_mark:
Alex Liu: Thanks everyone. Please @me when ticket moves. Happy to provide any extra docs.
Maria Gomez: Noted — tagging you on the ticket. We'll close the loop once payroll confirms the off-cycle or refund. :thumbsup:
PayrollBot: Ticket #PAY-7892 status: acknowledged by payroll ops. Estimated response: 1-2 business days.
